purpose: Verify the accounts-payable browser path from confirmed receipt through supplier invoice, payment, allocation and cleared aging. Check supplier permissions, currency selection, validation, original-event recovery after refresh, account isolation, and browser and API errors. The credit note case verifies draft validation, operation replay, confirmation, applying, reversing and voiding credits.
data: One private migrated MySQL schema and one localhost application. Three synthetic identities including a disabled bootstrap account, one supplier, one additional test currency, one SKU and UOM link, and one purchase order with one confirmed goods receipt line for HKD 325. The scenario also creates a no-PO draft and tests rejected payment data and one original-event replay. The separate credit scenario uses one synthetic supplier, two invoices and two original invoice lines. Both cases receive independently migrated disposable schemas.
concurrency: One Playwright worker, two functional cases executed serially, zero retries. Each case sends its own bounded intentional fault-injection and recovery requests.
repetitions: 1 per local invocation at each verification timezone.
thresholds: The browser case passes, one committed payment exists after retry, allocation clears outstanding aging, and the browser records no unexpected AP API or console errors. Routine coverage floors stay the same. The credit scenario verifies exact invoice and credit balances, replay, and no unexpected AP API or browser errors.
trigger: Explicit local functional validation using the dedicated Playwright config. Existing routine CI workflows, browser commands, discovery and worker counts are unchanged.
cost: The two local cases took 22.6 seconds in UTC and 23.8 seconds in Asia/Hong_Kong, including per-case schema setup. This adds no routine CI browser workload.
